title: Check yourself: Examples, tests, the interview and feedback

blocks.text: Questions on what this page has just taught. Choose one answer for each.

questions.stem: A conversion routine keeps being read in different ways, and each new version differs from the last. What should the next message contain?

options.text: A longer prose description with more adjectives
options.says: Ruled out because the guide's remedy for prose that is read in different ways is "concrete input and output examples".

options.text: The same description plus a request to be more careful
options.says: Ruled out because care does not say what is wanted, and "each correction is a guess at what was meant".

options.text: Two or three exact inputs paired with the outputs required
options.says: Exact examples remove the ambiguity that causes inconsistent reading.

options.text: A request to reproduce the previous version with small changes
options.says: Ruled out because small changes to a version that was misread repeat the misreading, while "the answer is nearly always the one that removes a guess".

origin.section: Examples, tests, the interview and feedback

questions.stem: The requirements of a large feature are unclear, and the developer is present at the keyboard. How should the work start?

options.text: Let Claude question them, then record a spec for later
options.says: The interview surfaces the requirements before any code, and the spec carries them into a clean session.

options.text: Write one long prompt that covers every case, then build
options.says: Ruled out because "do not start with a long prompt that guesses" at what the requirements are.

options.text: Have Claude pick the likeliest design, then build it
options.says: Ruled out because choosing alone skips the documented step: "ask Claude to interview you with AskUserQuestion".

options.text: Ask for the implementation, then repair whatever was misunderstood
options.says: Ruled out because repair means repeated correction, and "after two failed corrections the context is cluttered with failed approaches".
